Now, and for the future. The Program / Department / Team Mercy Corps is present in the DRC since August 2007 with a current workforce of more than 300 national and expatriate employees and operational presence in Goma and Beni (North Kivu Province), in Bunia (Ituri Province), and in Tshikapa, Kalonda West and Ndjoko Punda (Kasai Province), and representation in the capital city, Kinshasa. Mercy Corps is responding to the 17th Ebola outbreak in the DRC through an integrated emergency portfolio designed to support communities affected by the outbreak and strengthen the effectiveness of the wider response. COORDINATION, REPRESENTATION AND ADVOCACY Represent Mercy Corps strategically with the Ministry of Health and other government authorities, UN agencies, humanitarian coordination mechanisms, donors, international and national NGOs, local organizations and other relevant stakeholders. Work with the Country Director and relevant regional and global colleagues on high-level advocacy and policy engagement. Ensure consistent and transparent communication with donors and strategic partners. Where appropriate, represent Mercy Corps with national and international media and other external audiences. RESOURCE MOBILIZATION AND BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT Lead strategic resource mobilization for the Ebola response in close collaboration with the Country Director, Director of Programs, Business Development and Program Resource Manager, and relevant regional and global teams. Identify emerging funding opportunities and position Mercy Corps proactively with existing and prospective donors. Promote meaningful participation and leadership of local organizations and community-based actors where appropriate. Ensure that partner capacity strengthening is integrated into response planning where relevant. Identify and address partnership risks, performance issues and opportunities for improved collaboration. review_candidates.title: Delivery Network Assistant (Teaching)
review_candidates.description: We support peace and prosperity by building connections, understanding and trust between people in the UK and countries worldwide. For 90 years we have shaped brighter futures through education, arts, culture, language, and creativity. Working with people in over 200 countries and territories, we are on the ground in more than 100 countries. We connect. We inspire. Role purpose The purpose of this role is to provide essential logistical and administrative support to the Teaching Operations team , ensuring the smooth and efficient running of daily teaching activities. Reporting to the Teaching Operations Manager or Coordinator, the Assistant supports the preparation of teaching spaces, materials and equipment, assists with venue checks and other logistical arrangements, and completes routine administrative tasks such as data entry, filing and document preparation. The role responds to day-to-day operational needs and requests from teaching staff, helping maintain operational readiness and contributing to a high-quality learner and teacher experience. The role works closely with teaching staff and operational colleagues to ensure classrooms, materials, equipment and other resources are ready in advance of classes and that operational tasks are completed accurately and on time. The Assistant supports safeguarding and health & safety procedures through routine checks and reporting, and contributes to a positive, responsive and efficient working environment. The role requires strong attention to detail, responsiveness and a proactive approach to supporting the smooth execution of daily teaching operations. Role Accountabilities Customer Experience & Service Delivery : Receives and responds to customer enquiries, identifying complex issues that require resolution by others and referring them appropriately. Recognises the impact of incidents, including child protection incidents, behaviour management issues, complaints, resourcing problems, and logistical or technical difficulties, and proactively alerts the Team Leader to concerns that may affect service delivery or customer experience. Monitors the movement of Young Learner students during classes, ensuring they remain safe and on the premises, and escalates concerns to the Academic Team. Delivers administrative and customer services in line with agreed corporate procedures to maximise quality, continuity and efficiency. Provides logistical support for the organisation and delivery of teaching, registration, and other internal and external activities and events, including setting up classrooms in accordance with British Council standards and rearranging furniture and layouts with contracted staff. Proactively communicates and liaises with internal and external stakeholders to ensure effective coordination and delivery of services and activities. Administration, Facilities & Operational Support : Supports day-to-day operational and administrative requirements, including clerical work, filing, scanning, archiving, document and database updates, and maintaining accurate records relating to the work area. Supervises administrative and logistical services and assists the Marketing Officer with maintaining records of promotional materials. Ensures classroom IWBs are functioning correctly by carrying out basic troubleshooting and escalating technical issues to the IT Technician as required. Reports premises and equipment maintenance issues to the Business Operations team. Monitors small-scale resources, cash and stock in line with established procedures, ensuring equipment and materials are available and ready for use when required. Monitors the cleanliness of the British Council building, ensuring classrooms and public areas meet British Council standards, particularly during class changeovers and after-hours support, and reports service provider issues to the Business Operations team. Acts as the point of contact for deliveries to the Teaching Centre. Planning, Suppliers & Self-Management : Plans and prioritises own work activities, responding to changing requirements to ensure effective delivery of responsibilities across daily and weekly time horizons. Coordinates external contractors and suppliers to complete straightforward, time-limited activities in line with established procedures, monitoring completion against agreed quality and time standards to ensure efficient service delivery. Supports effective coordination of suppliers and services and maintains operational readiness by ensuring agreed activities, resources and logistical requirements are completed accurately and on time. Essentials Qualification and Experience High School Certificate University Graduate or Diploma in any field Minimum of 1 year of full-time work experience Desirable Experience of working in an educational institution Important information British Council Pay band: 2 Contract type: FTC Location: Egypt Proof of Identity requirements & right to work in the country: You must have the legal right to work in the stated location. Visa sponsorship and relocation assistance are not provided. Application Closing Date: Monday, 28 September 2026 at 20:30 Egypt time (23:59 IST) A connected and trusted UK in a more connected and trusted world. Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Statement We are committed to equality, diversity and inclusion and welcome applications from all sections of the community as we believe that a diverse workforce gives added depth to our work. The British Council is a Disability Confident Employer. The Disability Confident scheme helps challenge attitudes, increase understanding of disability and ensure staff are drawn from the widest possible pool of talent. We guarantee an interview for disabled applicants who meet the minimum role requirements. We welcome discussions about specific requirements or adjustments to enable participation and engagement in our work and activities. Safeguarding Statement The British Council is committed to safeguarding children, young people and adults who we work with. We believe that all children and adults everywhere in the world deserve to live in safe environments and have the right to be protected from all forms of abuse, maltreatment and exploitation as set out in article 19, UNCRC (United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child) 1989. Appointment to positions where there is direct involvement with vulnerable groups will be dependent on thorough checks being completed in line with legal requirements and with the British Council’s Safeguarding policies for Adults and Children.
